newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa's first oilfield shows potential - minister.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa's first oilfield shows potential - minister.

text.p: South Africa's first producing oilfield showed the potential of the country's vast, largely unexplored offshore acreage which could attract more local and international oil companies, Minerals and Energy Minister Penuell Maduna said on Thursday.
Speaking at a function to mark the production of the first oil from South Africa's offshore Oribi oilfield, Maduna said he was well aware that South Africa's offshore areas were also high risk areas.
"But Oribi shows that the rewards are certainly there for those who are prepared to take the necessary risk," he said.
It should attract other oil companies to prospect for oil and gas, thereby not only accelerating the search but also ensuring that offshore areas were thoroughly examined, he said.
"Hopefully, such a thorough examination will lead to further economic discoveries, for it is known that much of our area is as yet under-explored, or not explored at all."

Oribi, in which Energy Africa has a 20 percent stake alongside state oil firm Soekor, started pumping oil on May 12 and the first oil is expected to arrive at the Caltex Ltd oil refinery in Cape Town in early June.
Oribi should produce about 20 million barrels at the rate of about 20,000 barrels a day over four years.
Maduna also made a sharp attack on critics who believed that the state's oil assets should be sold to existing, white-owned oil companies.

"Those who think that we shall simply throw away such state resources and benefit only the apartheid-infested and apartheid-riven private sector with its known track record in the inequitable distribution of resources, opportunities, wealth and income might as well begin to eat their hearts out," he said.

"We want to use these assets in conjunction with the private sector primarily to create opportunities to empower ordinary people, especially those who in the past were confined to the realm of purveyors of cheap labour solely because of their race and skin colour," he said.
